Rashi on Pesachim 28b:10:1.hebrew: לקובעו חובה - האי "שבעת ימים תאכלו מצות" לאו לאקושי איסור חמץ למצות אכילת מצה אתא, אלא לאקושי אכילת מצה לאזהרת חמץ — לקבוע אכיל' מצה חובה לדורות, כל זמן שהוא מוזהר על החמץ, ואפילו בזמן שאין פסח. דלא תימא: "על מצות ומרורים יאכלוהו" כתיב — אי איכא פסח מיחייב באכילת מצה, ואי לא, לא:
Rashi on Pesachim 28b:10:1.english: To establish it as an obligation - This [verse], “Seven days you shall eat matzot,” does not come to juxtapose the prohibition of leavened bread to the mitzvah of eating matzah, but rather to juxtapose the eating of matzah to the prohibition against leavened bread — to establish the eating of matzah as an obligation for [all] generations, as long as one is cautioned against leavened bread, and even at a time when there is no Paschal offering; so that you should not say: It is written, “they shall eat it with matzot and bitter herbs” — if there is a Paschal offering, one is obligated to eat matzah, and if not, [one is] not.

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:11:1.hebrew: בערב תאכלו מצות - קרא יתירה הוא, דהא כתיב: "על מצות ומרורים יאכלוהו":
Rashi on Pesachim 28b:11:1.english: In the evening you shall eat matzot - It is a superfluous verse, for behold, it is written: “They shall eat it with matzot and bitter herbs.”

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:11:2.hebrew: לטמא ושהיה בדרך רחוקה - שאף על פי שאינו עושה פסח, חייב באכילת מצה:
Rashi on Pesachim 28b:11:2.english: For [one who is] ritually impure or was on a distant journey - That even though he does not bring the Paschal offering, he is obligated to eat matza.

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:11:3.english: He should not eat - He is not liable.

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:12:1.english: An uncircumcised man - [One] whose brothers died on account of circumcision.

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:12:2.hebrew: בן נכר - מי שנתנכרו מעשיו לאביו שבשמים, ולא לכל התורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 28b:12:2.english: A stranger - One whose deeds have become estranged from his Father in Heaven, and not [an apostate] with regard to the entire Torah.

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:12:3.hebrew: כתיב בהאי - ערל ובן נכר, וכתיב טמא ושהיה בדרך רחוקה דליכול מצות, ואף על גב דמצי יליף מיניה. הלכך, איצטריך היקישא לקובעו חובה. ומקראי אחריני טובא — כגון ״שבעת ימים מצות תאכלו״, וכגון ״מצות יאכל את שבעת הימים״ — לא נפקא ליה קביעות חובה, דהנהו לאו חובה נינהו, אלא: מצות יאכל ולא חמץ, ואם רצה ליזון שלא מחמץ ושלא ממצה — הרשות בידו. ותדע, דהא בכולהו כתיב ״את שבעת הימים״, וחובת מצה אינו אלא לילה הראשון, כדילפינן בפרק בתרא. אבל מההוא קרא נפקא לן חובת לילה הראשון, מדכתיב להיקישא גבי פסח, וכדכתיב ״תאכל עליו מצות״: כי פסח — לילה הראשון, אף היקישא שלא בזמן פסח — ללילה ראשונה. ואהני היקישא לקובעו חובה בזמן הזה, ואהני ״עליו״ למימרא דקביעת חובה דהיקישא לאו לכל שבעה, אלא ללילה הראשון:
Rashi on Pesachim 28b:12:3.english: It is written regarding this [one] - [Regarding] an uncircumcised man and an apostate; and it is written [regarding] one who is ritually impure or was on a distant journey, that he should eat matzot, even though he could have derived [one] from the other. Therefore, the juxtaposition was necessary to establish it as an obligation [nowadays]. And from many other verses — such as “Seven days you shall eat matzot” (Exodus 12:15), and such as “Matzot shall be eaten throughout the seven days” (Exodus 13:7) — establishing it as an obligation is not derived by him, for those are not an obligation; rather, [their meaning is:] matzot shall be eaten and not leaven, but if one wished to nourish himself without leaven and without matzah, he has permission [to do so]. And you may know [that this is so], for in all of them it is written “the seven days,” whereas the obligation of matzah is only [on] the first night, as we derive in the final chapter. However, from that verse [Deuteronomy 16:3], the obligation of the first night is derived for us: since the juxtaposition is written in connection with the Paschal offering, and as it is written, “You shall eat matzot with it” — just as [the] Pesach [offering is eaten only on] the first night, so too the juxtaposition [establishing an obligation] when it is not the time of the Pesach [offering applies only] to the first night. And the juxtaposition serves to establish it as an obligation in this era, and [the word] “with it” serves to say that the establishment of the obligation via the juxtaposition is not for all seven [days], but rather for the first night.

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:1:1.hebrew: ומשעה שאסור באכילה - היינו משש שעות ולמעלה, דאמרן לפני זמנו בלאו. והא מילתא רבי יהודה קאמר לה, כדמפרש בגמרא: אתאן לתנא קמא:
Rashi on Pesachim 28b:1:1.english: And from the time that it is prohibited to eat - That is, from six hours and onward, as we said: “Before its time” [is prohibited] by a negative commandment. And this matter, Rabbi Yehuda said it, as [the Gemara] explains in the Gemara: “We have come to the first tanna.”

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:1:2.hebrew: תמה על עצמך וכו' - דאפילו בתוך המועד קאמר דמותר בהנאה, וקא מתמה אהני דאסרי:
Rashi on Pesachim 28b:1:2.english: Be astounded with yourself, etc. - For he is saying that even during the Festival it is permitted to derive benefit [from it], and he is expressing astonishment at those who forbid [it].

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:2:1.hebrew: לא תאכל עליו - משעת שחיטה, דהיינו משש שעות ולמעלה, שחמה נוטה להעריב. הכי גרסינן: חמץ — אין לי אלא שנתחמץ מאליו:
Rashi on Pesachim 28b:2:1.english: You shall eat no leavened bread with it - From the time of the slaughter [of the Paschal lamb], that is, from the sixth hour and onward, when the sun inclines toward evening. This is the reading: “[From the word] chametz, I have [derived] only [that which] became leavened on its own.”

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:6:1.english: From where [is it derived regarding] the Passover of Egypt - That they observed the prohibition of leaven regarding it for only one day.

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:6:2.hebrew: ת"ל לא יאכל חמץ וסמיך ליה היום אתם יוצאים - לא יאכל חמץ היום:
Rashi on Pesachim 28b:6:2.english: The verse states: “Leavened bread shall not be eaten,” and juxtaposed to it: “This day you go forth” - [As if to say:] “Leavened bread shall not be eaten today.”

Rashi on Pesachim 28b:8:1.hebrew: ואי בעית אימא סמוכין לא דריש - רבי יהודה, אלא במשנה תורה לחוד. והכי שמעינן ליה בפרק קמא דיבמות (ד' ד.). הלכך, לית ליה דרבי יוסי הגלילי:
Rashi on Pesachim 28b:8:1.english: And if you wish, say: He does not expound juxtapositions - [That is,] Rabbi Yehuda [does not expound them] except in Mishneh Torah [Deuteronomy] alone. And so we have heard him [say] in the first chapter of Yevamot (daf 4a). Therefore, he does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:12:1.hebrew: כל ערל לא יאכל בו וכל בן נכר לא יאכל בו בו הוא אינו אוכל אבל אוכל הוא במצה ומרור - תימה: גבי בן נכר, שהוא מומר, אמאי איצטריך קרא? פשיטא שחייב לאכול מצה, דהא חייב בכל מצות האמורות בתורה! ואי קמשמע לן דמצי אכיל מצה אע"ג דאסור בפסח — הא נמי פשיטא, דאטו מצה קדושה אית בה?! וי"ל: דאיצטריך להיכא דנשחט הפסח כשהיה מומר ועשה תשובה, דאף על גב דלא אכיל בפסח — דאין נאכל אלא למנויו — מכל מקום חייב לאכול מצה ומרור:
Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:12:1.english: “No uncircumcised person shall eat of it,” and “no alien shall eat of it” — “of it” he does not eat, but he does eat matza and bitter herbs - [This is] puzzling: Regarding an alien [ben nekhar], who is an apostate, why was a verse necessary? It is obvious that he is obligated to eat matza, for he is obligated in all the mitzvot stated in the Torah! And if [the verse] comes to teach us that he may eat matza even though he is forbidden [to partake] of the Paschal offering — that too is obvious! For is there sanctity in matza?! And one can say [in resolution]: It was necessary for [a case] where the Paschal offering was slaughtered when he was an apostate and he repented; for even though he may not eat of the Paschal offering — since it is eaten only by those registered for it — nevertheless, he is obligated to eat matza and bitter herbs.

Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:12:2.hebrew: ערל - פי' הקונטרס: שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה. ולפירושו, פסול נמי בתרומה, דבהערל (יבמות ע. ושם) יליף תרומה מפסח בגז"ש דתושב ושכיר. והא דמיבעיא לן התם (דף עא): ערל קטן מהו לסוכו שמן של תרומה? ערלה שלא בזמנה פוסלת או לא? — יש לחלק בין שלא בזמנה דקטן, שאין חייב למול כיוצא בו, למתו אחיו מחמת מילה, דכיוצא בו חייבין. ותדע, דהא טומטום אינו אוכל בתרומה בפרק הערל (יבמות עב.), אף על גב דמסברא אין חייב לקרוע; הוא הדין מתו אחיו מחמת מילה, דאינו אוכל, אף על גב דאינו חייב למול:
Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:12:2.english: An uncircumcised man - Rashi explains: [This refers to one] whose brothers died as a result of circumcision. And according to his explanation, [such a person] is disqualified also from [eating] terumah, for in [the chapter entitled] HaArel (Yevamot 70a, and there), [the Gemara] derives [the disqualification of an uncircumcised person from] terumah from the Paschal offering via a gezeirah shavah of "resident" and "hired worker." And as for that which we raise as a dilemma there (daf 71a): What is the law regarding an uncircumcised minor, whether [one may] anoint him with terumah oil? Does uncircumcision not in its designated time disqualify, or not? — one can distinguish between [uncircumcision] not in its designated time in the case of a minor, where one like him is not obligated to be circumcised, and [one] whose brothers died as a result of circumcision, where one like him is obligated. And know [that this distinction is correct], for behold, a tumtum does not eat terumah in the chapter [entitled] HaArel (Yevamot 72a), even though logically he is not obligated to tear [open his membrane]; the same applies to [one] whose brothers died as a result of circumcision, that he does not eat [terumah], even though he is not obligated to circumcise.

Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:1:1.hebrew: רבי שמעון אומר חמץ לפני זמנו ולאחר זמנו אינו עובר עליו בלא כלום - נראה דלרבי שמעון, נהי דאין עובר עליו בלאו דחמץ לפני זמנו, מודה הוא דאסור באכילה משש שעות ולמעלה; מדאמרינן בפ"ק (לעיל פסחים דף יד.): "אין שורפין תרומה טהורה עם הטמאה", משמע: הא לבדה שורפין בשש, ואי מותרת לאכול יאכלנה עד הלילה! ועוד, דקאמר: "משעה שאסור באכילה אסור בהנאה, אתאן לת"ק" — מכלל דלרבי שמעון אסור באכילה, אע"פ שאינו אסור בהנאה, דהיינו אחר שש. ונראה דנפקא ליה מ"תשביתו" ומ"אך חלק", ומשמע "תשביתו" שלא כדרך הנאה, דהיינו אכילה; אבל להסיקו תחת תבשילו מותר לרבי שמעון. וא"ת: למה שורפין בשש? לרבי שמעון, יסיקנו עד הלילה מעט מעט תחת תבשילו! וי"ל: דגזרינן שמא יאכלנו. וכן לרבי יוסי הגלילי, דשרי חמץ להסיקו תחת תבשילו — היינו הכל ביחד, אבל מעט מעט לא, שמא יאכלנו; דמסתמא אית ליה: "אור לארבעה עשר בודקין וכו'":
Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:1:1.english: "Rabbi Shimon says: Leaven before its time and after its time, one does not transgress any [prohibition] on its account" - It appears that according to Rabbi Shimon, although one does not transgress a negative commandment of leaven before its time, he agrees that it is prohibited to eat from six hours and onward; from that which we say in the first chapter (above, Pesachim 14a): "We do not burn ritually pure terumah with ritually impure [terumah]," which implies: on its own, however, one burns [it] at six [hours]; and if it were permitted to eat, let him eat it until nightfall! And furthermore, since [the Gemara] states: "From the time that it is prohibited to eat, it is prohibited to derive benefit — we have come to the first tanna," this implies that according to Rabbi Shimon it is prohibited to eat, even though it is not prohibited to derive benefit, which is after six [hours]. And it appears that he derives this from "you shall eliminate" (Exodus 12:15) and from [the exposition that] "akh" divides [the day]; and "you shall eliminate" implies not in the manner of [customary] benefit, which is eating, but kindling it under his cooked food is permitted according to Rabbi Shimon. And if you say: Why do we burn [it] at six [hours]? According to Rabbi Shimon, let him kindle it until nightfall little by little under his cooked food! And one can say: We decree [against this] lest he eat it. And similarly according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who permits leaven to be kindled under his cooked food, that is [only when kindling] all of it together, but little by little, no, lest he eat it; for he presumably holds: "On the evening of the fourteenth, one searches [for leaven] etc."

Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:3:1.hebrew: אם כן מה תלמוד לומר לא תאכל עליו - הלשון דחוק, ונראה לרשב"א דהכי פירושו: והלא כבר נאמר "תאכל עליו מצות", וההוא "עליו" ע"כ אאכילת פסח קאי; הכי נמי "לא תאכל עליו חמץ" קאי נמי אשעת אכילת פסח. וקשה: אמאי איצטריך קרא להכי? מהיכא תיתי שיהא בבל תאכל חמץ בי"ד? דהא כולהו קראי מצרכינן לקמן אליבא דרבי שמעון:
Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:3:1.english: “If so, what does the verse teach [by stating]: ‘You shall eat no leavened bread with it’?” - The phrasing is difficult, and it appears to the Rashba that this is its explanation: Is it not already stated: “You shall eat with it matzot”? And that [instance of] “with it” perforce refers to the eating of the Pesach offering; so too, “You shall eat no leavened bread with it” also refers to the time of the eating of the Pesach offering. And it is difficult: Why was a verse needed for this? From where would it have entered our minds that one would be subject to [the prohibition of] “You shall eat no leavened bread” on the fourteenth [of Nisan], seeing as we require all the verses below according to Rabbi Shimon?

Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:4:1.hebrew: וחד לפני זמנו - וא"ת: ולחזקיה, מנלן איסור הנאה לפני זמנו, דליכא אלא חד "לא יאכל", וההוא מסברא מוקמינן לתוך זמנו? ואור"י: כיון דחד מהנהו קראי משמע איסור הנאה — לא נחלק ביניהם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:4:1.english: “And one before its time” - And if you say: According to Chizkiyah, from where do we derive the prohibition of benefit before its time, for there is only one [verse that states] “shall not be eaten,” and that [verse], through logical deduction, we establish [as applying] during its time? And the Ri says: Since one of these verses indicates a prohibition of benefit, we do not differentiate between them.

Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:5:1.hebrew: מחמת דבר אחר - פי' ריב"א: מחמת דבר אחר — דלאו מינו; דעל ידי שאור מיקרי חמץ טפי משנתחמץ מאליו, כדמוכח בפרק כל המנחות (מנחות נב:). אלא כגון שנתחמץ על ידי שמרי יין, שמייבשין השמרים בתנור כאשר עושין בארץ אשכנז. ול"ד לעיסה שנילושה ביין, דלית ביה כרת ויש בה לאו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 28b:5:1.english: "Due to another substance" - Riva explained: "Due to another substance" [means] that is not of its own kind; for [dough leavened] by means of sourdough is called chametz even more than that which leavened on its own, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaMenachot (Menachot 52b). Rather, [it refers to a case] such as where it was leavened by means of wine dregs, as they dry the dregs in an oven, as they do in the land of Ashkenaz. And it is not comparable to dough kneaded with wine, for which there is no [penalty of] karet, yet there is a negative prohibition.
